label: TP
reason: Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) is alert-TP: the sink variable sql (line 65) constructs a query string by concatenating bar, which is populated from user-supplied HTTP parameter names via doSomething (lines 80-90). Integer arithmetic guarantees bar equals param (user input), leading to direct injection into the SQL statement. Alert 1 (java/xss) targets the HTML output sink (lines 68-71) where encodeForHTML is applied; per the balanced encoding policy, preference is given to alert-TP when attacker-controlled data reaches the sink despite encoding. The case label is TP driven by the confirmed SQL injection vulnerability in Alert 2.

evidence.note: SQL injection sink: sql variable defined with direct concatenation of bar into query string.
Data flow control: doSomething method sets bar equal to param (user input) due to integer math guarantee (500/42 + 196 = 207 > 200).
XSS sink: response.getWriter().println includes encodeForHTML(sql), but per policy attacker-controlled data reaching sink prefers alert-TP.
